title: Five-Minute Quickstart
content:
1. docker compose up -d
2. curl http://localhost:14800/readyz
3. curl http://localhost:14800/v1/version to inspect feature flags
4. PUT /v1/facts to store a fact
5. POST http://localhost:14801/mcp with tools/list to verify MCP
6. corecruxctl verify-store --data-dir ./data

title: First Connect for Agents
content: When an agent meets Crux Daemon for the first time, pick endpoints in this order: 1. same host: HTTP http://127.0.0.1:14800 and MCP http://127.0.0.1:14801/mcp; 2. tailnet host: Tailscale MagicDNS or 100.x.y.z tailnet IP with the same ports; 3. remote HTTPS reverse proxy only when the operator intentionally exposes the daemon outside localhost/tailnet. Never inline bearer tokens in URLs, hooks, or MCP config. Resolve auth from CRUX_AGENT_TOKEN, CRUX_AGENT_TOKENS, a token CSV such as ~/.config/cuecrux/crux-tokens/MCP_AGENT_TOKENS_CSV, or a host secret manager. Verify in order: GET /readyz, GET /v1/version, MCP initialize, tools/list, cuecrux_session, sync_status(), update_status(), get_bootstrap(topic="patterns", token_budget=500), then store_fact and query_facts(token_budget=500). If sync_status is local_only or degraded, keep using local HTTP/MCP and surface remote sync as optional follow-up. For Codex CLI, use native streamable HTTP MCP if it handshakes; if not, configure integrations/codex-cli/crux-mcp-stdio.py as a stdio bridge named crux. The bridge tries CRUX_MCP_URLS, CRUX_MCP_URL, ~/.config/cuecrux/env, then localhost.

title: Local-Only Mode
content: If sync_status reports mode=local_only or mode=degraded, do not block the user. Crux Daemon still provides a local fact store, local session store, HTTP API, and MCP tools on this node. Continue storing facts and sessions locally, tell the user remote sync is not available yet, and only treat sync as optional follow-up work.

title: Choosing HTTP vs MCP
content: Use HTTP when the host system needs shared app state or service-to-service calls: /v1/facts, /v1/sessions, /v1/version. Use MCP when the agent needs private facts, agent-scoped sessions, handoff, or tool discovery. Many systems use both: HTTP for shared product data and MCP for per-agent memory.

title: Human-Assisted Integration
content: Use this when the agent cannot edit the host system directly. 1. Ask the operator which surface they need: HTTP, MCP, or both. 2. Give them the exact endpoint, auth token/header, and env vars to set. 3. Tell them to verify with /v1/version for HTTP and tools/list or get_agent_identity for MCP. 4. Finish by storing and retrieving one fact as an end-to-end check.

title: Automatic Integration
content: Use this when the agent can edit the host application or runtime config. 1. Detect whether the target integration needs shared HTTP state, MCP agent memory, or both. 2. Write the base URL, auth config, and MCP bearer token into the target system. 3. Reload or restart the host application. 4. Verify with /v1/version, tools/list, store_fact, and query_facts. 5. If remote sync is desired later, add CORECRUXD_SYNC_REMOTE_URL and CORECRUXD_SYNC_API_KEY, then re-check sync_status.

title: Human-Assisted Upgrade
content: Use this when the agent can inspect the node but cannot change the service itself. 1. Call update_status() or inspect /v1/version.update. 2. If state=behind, ask the operator to snapshot CORECRUXD_DATA_DIR or take an equivalent volume snapshot before touching git. 3. Tell them to run git fetch, git pull on the tracked branch, rebuild, and restart the service. 4. Verify with /v1/version, update_status(), tools/list, and one fact round-trip. 5. If state=ahead or diverged, do not ask for a blind pull; tell the operator to review local commits first.

title: Automatic Upgrade
content: Use this only when the agent can edit the checkout and restart the service safely. 1. Call update_status(). Proceed automatically only when state=behind, the repo_dir is writable, and a backup path exists. 2. Pull get_bootstrap(topic="docs", query="backup") and complete one backup action first: filesystem snapshot, receipt export, or another operator-approved snapshot. 3. Run git fetch and git pull for the tracked branch, rebuild, and restart the service. 4. Verify /v1/version.update moved to current (or closer to current), then verify tools/list, store_fact, and query_facts. 5. If state=ahead, diverged, unavailable, or error, stop and switch to the human-assisted upgrade playbook.

title: Backup and Rollback Options
content: Crux Daemon does not yet ship a one-click backup manager, but there are operator-grade backup rails. Before upgrades, prefer: 1. Filesystem or volume snapshots of CORECRUXD_DATA_DIR (ZFS/LVM/cloud volume snapshot). 2. corecruxctl verify-store --data-dir ./data --scope recent before and after the change. 3. Receipt or replay exports from /v1/replay/exports/* for audit and recovery evidence. 4. Git branch or tag markers before pulling when the service runs from a checkout. Roll back by restoring the snapshot and restarting the previous binary, not by deleting live data ad hoc.

title: Appending Events
content: POST /v1/admin/append (or compatibility alias /v1/append) with tenant_id, stream_type, stream_id, and events array. Each event needs event_id, occurred_at (RFC3339), event_type, and payload (JSON string). Default Crux Daemon runtime leaves the dataplane disabled, so append requires a dataplane-enabled deployment.

title: Text Search
content: POST /v1/query/text-search with tenant_id and query. Optional: token_budget (fill until budget), min_score (relevance floor), mode=scan (metadata only).

title: Fact Store
content: PUT /v1/facts to store. GET /v1/facts?query=... to search. GET /v1/facts/entity/{name} by entity. DELETE /v1/facts/{id} to soft-delete.

title: Session Store
content: PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/state with JSON body. GET /v1/sessions/{id}/state to retrieve. State persists across requests within the session.

title: Architecture
content: 14 Rust crates. corecruxd serves HTTP on 14800, gRPC on 4007, and built-in MCP on 14801 by default. Append-only event store with sealed segments. .ccxi companion indexes for BM25. CROWN receipts on every operation.

title: Configuration
content: All config via environment variables. CORECRUXD_DATA_DIR (data), CORECRUXD_HTTP_PORT (default 14800), CORECRUXD_BUILD_CCXI (index building), CORECRUXD_QUERY_TEXT_SEARCH (enable search). Optional upstream sync uses CORECRUXD_SYNC_ENABLED, CORECRUXD_SYNC_REMOTE_URL, CORECRUXD_SYNC_API_KEY, and CORECRUXD_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS. Git-based update checks use CORECRUXD_UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED, CORECRUXD_UPDATE_CHECK_REMOTE, CORECRUXD_UPDATE_CHECK_REF, CORECRUXD_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS, and optionally CORECRUXD_UPDATE_CHECK_REPO_DIR. If sync is unset, Crux Daemon runs local-only by default.
